candidates.review_note: The cumulative requests minus returns minus initial stock is the net deficit. Its positive part is exactly the number waiting, so total waiting time is its area over consecutive event intervals. A positive final deficit gives infinite waiting. Sort deficit levels and precompute suffix duration and deficit-duration sums to evaluate each stock query in logarithmic time. Earlier surplus is retained; no artificial clipping of cumulative balance occurs.

A valid single polyline visits each original segment exactly once in one of two orientations. The sum of original segment lengths is constant; subset dynamic programming minimizes only added connectors, recording the outgoing endpoint of the last segment. Every segment and either orientation may start without connector cost; no closing edge is added because the requested object is a polyline, not a cycle. Euclidean lengths and five-decimal formatting follow the source.
